newsitem.title: USA: Dlr closes mixed in U.S. in thin yearend trade.
newsitem.headline: Dlr closes mixed in U.S. in thin yearend trade.

text.p: The dollar ended mixed in light trade while dealers were reluctant to participate before Christmas holiday departures and the tallying of the year's profit on December 31.

"People are not really too interested in giving up money," said James Powers, vice president at Westdeutsche Landesbank Girozentrale in New York. "If they have had a good year they'll keep their money; if they had a bad year, why risk more? It is so close to the end of the year."
Volume was extemely light, and last minute paring of dollar/mark holdings was barely counteracted by buying.
On Friday, the dollar declined to 1.5515/20 marks, from 1.5565/75 at the open. But dollar/yen hovered over 114 during the session, closing at 114.32/37 just up from 114.27/32.

With the market trying to keep dealings to a minimum before yearend, traders said they were more interested in talking about holiday plans. For many, Friday is the last day before before a one-week vacation and most trading centers are closed for at least two days next week.
Christmas day falls on Wednesday but markets in Germany are also shut for three days including Christmas Eve and the day after Christmas.

"Typically a very illiquid time in our market these next two weeks," said Stephen Flanagan, vice president at Credit Agricole, in New York. "I think people have done a lot of perhaps squaring up of positions, which ... would have been long-dollars."
Meanwhile, a weak Japanese economy and sputtering stock market weighed on the Japanese currency, with dollar buy orders reported below 114 yen. But offers above 114.30 kept dollar gains in check.

In an effort to ensure the economy stays on the path to recovery, the Japanese government on Friday approved supplementary budget spending totalling 2.67 trillion yen ($23.4 billion) for the fiscal year ending next March 31.

On Friday, the Nikkei 225 average, Japan's key stock index, did manage to regain some of the ground lost the day before, but the average still ended below the crucial 20,000 level which it punctured Thursday, making a low for the year.

But the dollar was unable to make much headway, with Japanese investors reportedly needing to sell dollars to protect their U.S. bond holdings against a depreciation of the U.S. currency. Traders also said further yen weakness against the dollar could take a toll on the already fragile Japanese stock market.

"It's a situation where a higher dollar/yen from this point on could have a negative implication for Nikkei stocks," said Jeffrey Yu, senior dealer at Sanwa Bank in New York. "Therefore, everybody's trading very cautiously about a higher dollar."
The dollar fell to 1.3335/45 Swiss francs from 1.3375/85 at the open. But it rose to Canadian $1.3674/79 from C$1.3670/75.
The pound rose to $1.6698/08 from $1.6630/40. The Australian dollar slipped to $0.7948/53 from $0.7951/56.
